notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l001: The opening word is provisionally read Үрөндөй; the verb may be a nearby form.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l003: The middle words атан орук are difficult; translation follows the apparent sense of a settled camp.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l004: The word миңдей is a provisional reading of the compact final phrase.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l005: Тобочокон is treated as a proper name but its exact spelling is uncertain.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l006: Both words are provisional visual readings; the English only gives a possible sense.

notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l009: The opening form and final verb are difficult; both are retained as seen.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l010: каргы is a provisional reading, understood as an epithet for the enemy.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l011: The compound дүйнөкү is visually uncertain; translation follows дүйнө, ‘world or realm.’
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l015: The final word is provisionally read төөчү; its intended verb may differ.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l018: The first word could be a nearby form; коргон салалы is comparatively clear.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l019: The phrase бир ага турмак is provisional; translation follows its apparent contrastive sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l020: The syntax of жери ага is unresolved; оюн алалык is read literally as ‘let us take or learn the intent.’
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l021: чаргын is a provisional visual reading and may name their condition or disposition.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l022: кайып is visually plausible but the idiom is uncertain.

notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l025: The case ending and final converb are faint but this is the closest reading.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l027: The final form is retained as written; the subject and aspect are inferred from context.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l029: The final noun is provisionally read чегирин, ‘boundary.’
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l030: аркан is clear enough visually but may be a different modifying word; English conveys the apparent terrain sense.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l031: Opening Боп may be part of a longer or differently spelled form.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l033: A short standalone manuscript baseline; its syntax continues into the following line.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l034: The phrase делиптен заада кыл is difficult; translation gives the apparent instruction to identify them.
notes.sayakbay-ms-current146:pdf052:l035: The first noun may be a nearby form; the remainder is comparatively clear.
